summary: Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a sinologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1967–1969) and the University of Munich (~1969–1973), later holding posts at Munich (~1981–1993) and Göttingen (~1993–2015).

Hemchandra Raychaudhuri was an Indologist and historian who taught Jitendra Nath Banerjea. He served at the University of Calcutta as Carmichael Professor and Head of the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture (attested 1939 and 1965).
Hemendra Nath Chakravarty was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Gopinath Kaviraj. He held a post at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.
Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri is a linguist and Indologist. He held a post as professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1991 and 2026).

Hendrik Arent Hamaker studied at the Athenaeum Illustre of Amsterdam (~1807–1812). A linguist, he served as Professor of Arabic, Chaldaean, and Syriac at the University of Franeker (1815–1817) and held professorships at Leiden University from 1817 and 1822–1835.
Hendrik van Gelder was an historian and archaeologist. He held posts at Utrecht University from 1906 to 1915 and at Leiden University from 1915 to 1921.

Henepola Gunaratana, a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, studied at Vidyasekhara Pirivena, Buddhist Missionary College, Kelaniya, and American University (BA, PhD), under teachers including Kiribatkumbure Sonuttara. He led the Buddhist Institute of Kuala Lumpur and held posts at American, Georgetown, Bucknell, and Maryland.

Heng Sure studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union (PhD under Ronald Y. Nakasone), and also studied under Hsuan Hua. A Buddhist studies scholar, he has held professorships at GTU, Bond University, and Dharma Realm Buddhist University.

Heng Yin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed a doctoral degree at Yunnan University (2018–2025). In 2023, he held an assistant professor post at China West Normal University.

Henk Blezer, a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, studied at Leiden University (1987–1997). He held posts at Leiden University as a postdoctoral researcher (1993–1997) and lecturer (2002–2008), and at the International Institute for Asian Studies (1997–2001).

Henk Bodewitz studied at Utrecht University (~1957–1973, PhD under Jan Gonda). A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he held posts at Utrecht University (assistant professor 1966, chair of Sanskrit 1976–1992) and Leiden University (associate professor ~1966–1976, professor 1992–2002).
Henk J. Verkuyl is a linguist who studied at Utrecht University from ~1960 to 1972 and later held an academic post there from ~1981 to 2003.

Henri Arvon, a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Strasbourg. He taught at Prytanée National Militaire (~1956–1965), University of Clermont-Ferrand (1966–1971), and Paris Nanterre University (~1965–1982) as a professor.

Henri Bergson was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Condorcet, the École Normale Supérieure (~1878–1881), and the University of Paris (~1888–1889). He held posts at Lycée David d'Angers (~1881–1883) and the Collège de France (1900–1904).

Henri Cordier studied at Lycée Chaptal (~1861–1867). Working in sinology and history, he served as librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society North China Branch (1871) and as professor at Sciences Po (~1886–1925) and Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1888).

Henri Deydier was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied under Jean Przyluski, Henri Maspero, and Alfred Foucher, and earned a diploma from the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1946–1950) before joining the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 1950.

Henri Frei, a linguist and Japanologist, studied at INALCO and the University of Geneva (PhD under Charles Bally; also under Manu Leumann). He held posts at Peking University (1933–1934), Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1934–1938), and Geneva (1940–1969).

Henri Gaidoz, a scholar of linguistics and religious studies, studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber (1865). He taught geography and ethnography at École Libre des Sciences Politiques (1872–1908) and Celtic philology at École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 1876).
Henri Hauvette studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand from ~1878 to 1885. He subsequently held academic posts at Grenoble Alpes University (~1895–1906) and the University of Paris (~1906–1935).

Henri Hubert, a historian and religious studies scholar, studied at the ENS and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi. He was conservateur adjoint at the National Archaeological Museum (~1898–1927), professor at École du Louvre (1906), and directeur d’études at EPHE (1907).
